pick.name: Ghostty
pick.what: GPU-accelerated native terminal, fast and low-config
pick.why: Fast, native UI, MIT, strong defaults; works well with Claude Code
pick.install: brew install --cask ghostty (macOS; community cask of the official dmg); apt install ghostty (Ubuntu 26.04+) or distro package (Arch, Fedora COPR, Nix, Snap, etc.)

alts.name: Windows Terminal
alts.why: Best terminal on Windows; zero config

alts.name: WezTerm
alts.why: Only candidate here with identical builds on macOS, Windows and Linux
alts.install: brew install --cask wezterm | winget install wez.wezterm

candidates.name: Ghostty
candidates.verdict: pick for macOS/Linux; no official Windows build

candidates.name: WezTerm
candidates.verdict: one config everywhere, but stale stable channel

candidates.name: Warp
candidates.verdict: all 3 OS, free plan exists, but bundles its own AI agent and account flow

decision: Terminal choice is OS-dependent: Ghostty on macOS and Linux, Windows Terminal on Windows. Choose WezTerm for one identical setup across machines, or iTerm2/Kitty if you already prefer them. Warp is optional: its built-in agent duplicates Claude Code.
details: Rebuilt from a Windows-only slot. Ghostty officially ships binaries only for macOS; Linux builds come from distro packagers; no Windows build.

os_notes.macOS: Ghostty (brew install --cask ghostty) or iTerm2; Terminal.app is fine too.
os_notes.Windows: Windows Terminal (preinstalled on Windows 11); Ghostty has no Windows build. It has no default desktop notification, so set Claude's preferredNotifChannel to terminal_bell.
os_notes.Linux: Ghostty is in Arch, Ubuntu 26.04, Nix, Snap and other distro repos; Kitty and WezTerm also work.

verify.note: Resolves the 'no stable tag' and licence unverified items. os_notes are correct.
